headline: Last session: Sensex and Nifty plunged as foreign investors sold stocks, marking the longest weekly losing run in years.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed for trading today due to an NSE holiday. It will reopen on Monday, 5 October.

why: Soaring bond yields and elevated oil prices
Global rate hike concerns sparking outflows
Market recording its eighth consecutive week of losses
whatHappening: NSE and BSE are closed today for Gandhi Jayanti; trading resumes on Monday, October 5
Sensex dropped 570 points in the last session, while Nifty closed at 22,421.95
Indian benchmark shares logged their worst monthly performance since March
Defence Secretary confirmed Akash Missile exports to Armenia, Tajikistan, and Turkmenistan
summary: Indian markets are closed today for Gandhi Jayanti following a sharp decline in the previous session where the Sensex fell 570 points. The market recorded its eighth straight week of losses, the longest streak in 25 years, driven by foreign fund outflows and rising bond yields. Investors remain cautious as benchmark indices post their worst monthly performance since March.
